conjecture: KP_y : EJ :: EJ : KP_y, i.e. the segment EJ cut off on the tangent g equals the distance of P_y from the line e: EJ = KP_y (= P_yF) for every P_x. In symptoma form: KD^2 = (2·FD)·VJ, i.e. the ordinate KD (= P_yH) is a mean proportional between the latus rectum 2·FD (= 4·VD) and the abscissa VJ = EJ − VE; hence P_y traces the parabola with focus F, directrix e and vertex V.
reason: FG is a diameter, so angle FED = 90°; V is the intersection of the tangents at E and F, so VE = VF, hence V is the circumcentre of the right triangle FED and VF = VD = VE = a (V is the midpoint of FD). The line h1 (through V, perpendicular to j) is the midline between F and the line e, so P_x is the midpoint of FK and m, perpendicular to FK at P_x, is the perpendicular bisector of FK; P_y on m therefore has P_yF = P_yK. Since P_yK is parallel to j, P_yK equals the distance of P_y to e, i.e. P_yK = HD. Because HJ is parallel to DE and both H and D lie on j, V is the centre of a similarity carrying D→H, E→J, so VJ = VH (and J lies on the opposite side of V from E); thus EJ = VE + VJ = VD + VH = HD = KP_y = P_yF. In coordinates (D origin, j the x-axis, VD = a, P_x at height t): P_y = (−a − t²/a, 2t), K = (0, 2t), so KD² = 4t² = 4a·(t²/a) = (2FD)·VH = (2FD)·VJ — the ordinate is the mean proportional between the latus rectum and the abscissa, the defining proportion of a parabola with focus F and directrix e.

conjecture: KP_y : EJ :: 1 : 1 for every P_x — i.e. the segment EJ cut on the tangent g is always equal to the segment KP_y (and both equal the focal distance FP_y); in Menaechmus' form the underlying symptoma is (P_yH)^2 = (4·VE)·VJ, the ordinate P_yH being a mean proportional between the latus rectum 4·VE and the abscissa VJ.
reason: Put F at the origin with j (the tangent at F) as the axis of abscissas and FG as the axis of ordinates. V is the pole of the chord EF, so VE = VF = v, and the chord GE through the antipode G meets j at D with FD = 2v, so V is the midpoint of FD and VD = VE = v. P_x lies on h1 (x = v) and K on e (x = 2v), so P_x is the midpoint of FK; the line m through P_x perpendicular to FK is the perpendicular bisector of FK, hence P_y (on m and on the parallel to j through K) satisfies P_yF = P_yK. Thus P_y traces the parabola with focus F and directrix e, vertex V, latus rectum 4v = 4·VE: if y = P_yH is the ordinate and VH the abscissa measured from V, then y^2 = 4·VE·VH. Since HJ is parallel to DE and VD = VE, triangle VHJ is isosceles, VJ = VH, so J simply carries the abscissa onto the tangent g, with J and E on opposite sides of V. Therefore EJ = VE + VJ = v + VH, while KP_y = FD − FH = 2v − (v − VH) = v + VH = P_yF. Hence EJ = KP_y for every position of P_x (numerically both are 11.345 = FP_y), the equality being a consequence of the proportion y^2 : VJ = 4·VE : 1 of the parabola.
